title: Causing death by negligence — BNS 2023 s.106

review.method: Encoded from the text of s.106. Deliberately small (30 cases): the point is the boundary with culpable homicide in ss.100-105 (separate pack in.bns.homicide) — s.106 applies only to a rash or negligent act 'not amounting to culpable homicide', so the encoding must say where that line falls and what it costs to move it.

in_scope: s.106(1) causing death by a rash or negligent act
s.106(2) causing death by dangerous driving or racing
out_of_scope: ss.100-105 culpable homicide and murder (separate pack in.bns.homicide)
ss.107-108 abetment of suicide (separate pack in.bns.abetment-suicide)
s.109 attempt to murder (separate pack in.bns.attempt-murder)
MV Act s.184 dangerous driving (no death)

sources.note: Assented 25 Dec 2023, in force 1 Jul 2024. India Code PDF.
Predecessor of s.106(1). The maximum rose from two years (IPC) to five years (BNS); s.106(2) has no IPC equivalent.

value_labels.rash_negligent: rash or negligent (conscious risk or inadvertence)

value_labels.ordinary_driving: driving, but not in a manner dangerous to human life and not racing
value_labels.dangerous_or_racing: driving in a manner dangerous to human life, or racing

terms.definition: Rash means a conscious taking of a risk; negligent means inadvertent failure to take care. Section 106 covers both, so the encoding treats them as one culpability value.

The boundary with ss.100-105: if the act was done with intention or knowledge of likely death, it is culpable homicide or murder, not s.106. Knowledge of mere possibility sits on the line and is recorded as an ambiguity.

branches.text: Whoever causes death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act ...
branches.notes: No death means s.106 is not engaged at all. Hurt, attempt and abetment are different provisions and outside this pack.

branches.text: by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide
branches.notes: Intention or knowledge of likely death is culpable homicide or murder (ss.100-105, separate pack), so s.106 is excluded by its own words. Knowledge of mere possibility is treated as rashness in the current encoding; the ambiguity records the other reading.

branches.text: by doing any rash or negligent act
branches.notes: A death without rashness or negligence (pure accident) is not s.106. The fault element is the whole offence.

branches.text: Whoever causes death of any person by driving a vehicle in a manner dangerous to human life, or by racing
branches.notes: The specific provision for road deaths. It has no IPC equivalent; before 2024 such deaths were prosecuted as IPC s.304A (two years) or under the MV Act.

branches.text: Whoever causes death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide
branches.notes: The general provision. Ordinary negligent driving that kills falls here; only dangerous driving or racing goes to s.106(2).

punishment_rules.text: Imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both [s.106(2)]
Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both [s.106(1)]

ambiguities.question: Does knowledge of the possibility of death amount to culpable homicide (ss.100-105), or is it still rashness under s.106?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: If knowledge of possibility is culpable homicide, those deaths leave s.106 entirely (and enter ss.100-105, where the maxima are far higher). If it is rashness, they stay in s.106 at five or ten years. Same facts, different offence and different ceiling.
ambiguities.position_a: Possibility is rashness: only knowledge of likelihood (or intention) is culpable homicide, so s.106 covers possibility-knowledge.
ambiguities.position_b: Possibility is culpable: anyone who foresees death as possible and proceeds is at least culpable, so s.106 excludes possibility-knowledge.

variants.label: possibility is rashness (current encoding, parameter is false)

illustrations.text: A rash act (not driving) causes a death without intention or knowledge of likely death: s.106(1).
Driving in a manner dangerous to human life causes a death: s.106(2), not s.106(1).
Dangerous driving without a death is not s.106, however rash.
An intentional killing is murder (ss.100-105), so s.106 is excluded by its own words.
A death without rashness or negligence (pure accident) is not s.106.
